required.asked_by: Report whether the subscription is assigned
required.rationale: used is true on this row and false on the neighbouring one, so the value discriminates. The forms are all multi-word: a bare "assigned" is a substring of "unassigned", which entangles it with the forbidden fact -- check_fact_entanglement caught exactly that, see the edit log
required.note: the seed carries `"used": true` as a JSON boolean; every natural English rendering of it ("is assigned", "in use") is therefore a derivation rather than a seed literal

required.asked_by: which RHDP project tag it is assigned to
required.rationale: the projecttag field; unguessable, and empty on the other seeded subscription

required.asked_by: name one that is free to hand out
required.rationale: the unassigned subscription. parsec's list_pools returns per-pool counts and no subscription names, so only get_pool on pool 01 surfaces it -- a call the contract does not pin, which a correct agent must still make

forbidden.rationale: an agent that reads the wrong row reports 389 as free. Every form names 389 explicitly, because the instruction now asks the agent to name an available subscription -- so a bare "is available" is a correct statement about pool-01-390 and must not be forbidden

counts.asked_by: say how many there are in total
counts.rationale: the size of the pools database. The subscription names contain 389 and 390, so a bare digit could coincide -- the noun-proximity rule is what makes 2 safe to accept here
